claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 omits the governing condition 'whenever an OSHA standard in this part requires one' from 29 CFR 1910.38(a), making the duty unconditional and overbroad.

Claim C0001 captures the general requirement for an emergency action plan to be in writing, kept in the workplace, and accessible, but its summary and scope omit the express exception allowing employers with 10 or fewer employees to communicate the plan orally.

Claim C0002 accurately represents the permission under 29 CFR 1910.38(b) for an employer with 10 or fewer employees to communicate the plan orally, retaining governing scope, actor, threshold, and modality.
Claim C0003 correctly states the training duty under 29 CFR 1910.38(e), retaining the parent scope from 1910.38(a), the mandatory force, the actor, and the actions.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 omits the conditional applicability requirement ('whenever an OSHA standard in this part requires one') and the application sentence of 1910.38(a).
Claim C0001 states the written plan mandate but fails to mention the explicit exception for employers with 10 or fewer employees.
Claim C0002 fully and faithfully covers the oral communication permission for employers with 10 or fewer employees.
The requirement for procedures for reporting a fire or other emergency under 1910.38(c)(1) is not represented in any draft claim.
The requirement for emergency evacuation procedures under 1910.38(c)(2) is not represented in the draft.
The requirement for critical plant operations procedures under 1910.38(c)(3) is omitted from the draft.
The requirement for post-evacuation accounting procedures under 1910.38(c)(4) is omitted from the draft.
The requirement for procedures for employees performing rescue or medical duties under 1910.38(c)(5) is omitted from the draft.
The requirement under 1910.38(c)(6) regarding names or job titles of contact persons is omitted from the draft.
The duty to have and maintain an employee alarm system under 1910.38(d) is omitted from the draft.
The distinctive signal and 1910.165 compliance requirement for alarm systems under 1910.38(d) is omitted from the draft.
Claim C0003 faithfully covers the duty to designate and train employees to assist in safe and orderly evacuation under 1910.38(e).
The plan review requirement upon plan development or initial job assignment under 1910.38(f)(1) is omitted from the draft.
The plan review requirement when employee responsibilities change under 1910.38(f)(2) is omitted from the draft.
The plan review requirement when the plan is changed under 1910.38(f)(3) is omitted from the draft.
